name: Nicaragua
summary_text: Nicaragua demands real caution from trans visitors. Nothing criminalises being trans (sodomy was decriminalised in 2008), but NGOs document 108 cases of violence against the LGTBIQ+ community in 2024 alone, and 10 murders of trans women in the last two and a half years. Since 2018 the Ortega regime has shut down or exiled virtually all independent civil society — including LGBT organisations — so there is no domestic protection infrastructure and no recourse; arbitrary detention is used broadly against perceived opponents.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Nicaragua: documents the legal status of same-sex conduct (decriminalised in 2008) and the absence of gender-recognition provisions.

sources.title: Nicaragua - F&M Global Barometers
sources.claim_summary: F&M Global Barometers country profile for Nicaragua: composite LGBT-rights perception scores including the Global Barometer of Transgender Rights index.

sources.title: Nicaragua - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Nicaragua: official assessment - no criminalisation but significant societal discrimination; the Ortega government's broader repression affects civil society including LGBT groups.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to Nicaragua's international human-rights environment.

sources.title: After a year of protest in Nicaragua, Ortega’s crackdown on the media continues - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (May 2019): after a year of protest, Ortega's crackdown continues - at least 325 dead, 2,000+ injured per the IACHR; journalist Miguel Mora describes being beaten by a pro-government mob and targeted partly for being gay - the intersection of political repression and homophobia.

sources.title: Nicaragua to decriminalise gay sex | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Nov 2007): Nicaragua to decriminalise gay sex - the new penal code (effective March 2008) removed the 1992 sodomy law, which had criminalised not only same-sex relationships but was vague enough to permit prosecution of LGBT-rights campaigning or providing sexual-health services.
